column1: comprehensive§The review was comprehensive in a way that helped nobody: eleven volumes, four years, and not one actionable recommendation.§这次评估**全面**得毫无用处——十一卷、四年，却没有一条可执行的建议。§com-（完全）+ prehend（抓，同 apprehend 领会）→ 全抓进来

compromise§The compromise satisfied neither side and held for thirty years, which is roughly the definition of a successful treaty.§这项**妥协**两边都不满意，却维持了三十年——这大致就是成功条约的定义。§com-（一起）+ promis（承诺，同 promise 承诺）→ 双方各让一步
compulsive§His compulsive checking of the figures caught two errors a week and cost him every evening he had.§他**强迫性地**核对数据，每周逮到两处错误，也搭上了自己所有的晚上。§com-（加强）+ puls（推，同 pulse 脉搏）→ 被推着不得不做
compunction§She dismissed the entire team without compunction, then wrote a memo praising the culture they had built.§她毫无**内疚**地解散了整个团队，随后写了份备忘录称赞他们建立的文化。§com-（加强）+ punct（刺，同 puncture 刺穿）→ 良心上扎一下
conceal§The report concealed the cost overrun in a footnote, which is where the auditor eventually found it two years later.§这份报告把超支**隐藏**在一条脚注里，两年后审计员正是在那儿找到了它。§con-（完全）+ ceal（藏，同 cell 密室）
concealment§Concealment, not the original mistake, ended his career: the error was survivable and the cover-up was not.§终结他职业生涯的是**隐瞒**而非最初的失误——错误还有得救，掩盖没有。§
concede§He conceded the point about timing and immediately used it to argue that the whole plan should be delayed.§他**承认**了关于时机的那一点，随即用它论证整个计划都该推迟。§con-（完全）+ ced（走开，同 recede 后退）→ 让开一步

conceivable§Every conceivable objection had already been raised in the 1970s, and the file containing them runs to nine hundred pages.§所有**想得到的**反对意见在 1970 年代就已提出过，收录它们的卷宗长达九百页。§con-（一起）+ ceiv（拿，同 receive 接收）→ 心里接得住

concentration§The concentration required is the real barrier: the task is simple, and forty uninterrupted minutes are nearly impossible to find.§真正的障碍是所需的**专注**——任务本身简单，可四十分钟不被打断几乎找不到。§con-（一起）+ centr（中心）
concession§The concession looked generous until someone read the schedule and saw that it expired in eleven months.§这项**让步**看着大方，直到有人读了附表，发现它十一个月后就失效。§
conciliatory§His conciliatory tone came four days too late, by which point both unions had already voted to strike.§他**息事宁人**的语气晚了四天，那时两个工会都已投票决定罢工。§con-（一起）+ cili ← cal（召唤，同 council 议会）→ 把人叫到一起
concise§The abstract is concise to the point of uselessness: eighty words that tell you the topic and nothing else.§这段摘要**简洁**到没用——八十个词只告诉你主题，别的什么也没有。§con-（完全）+ cis（切，同 scissors 剪刀）→ 切干净
conclusive§Nothing in the file is conclusive, and the case has been reopened three times on the same ambiguous evidence.§卷宗里没有一样是**决定性的**，这案子已因同一批模棱两可的证据重启过三次。§con-（完全）+ clus（关闭，同 include 包括）→ 把事情关死
concoct§He concocted an explanation involving a lost password, a broken laptop, and a cousin nobody had ever met.§他**编造**了一套说辞，牵扯到丢失的密码、坏掉的笔记本，还有一个谁也没见过的表亲。§con-（一起）+ coct（煮，同 decoct 熬煮）→ 一锅乱炖出来

concordance§The concordance between the two witnesses was suspiciously exact: identical wording, identical order, identical pauses.§两位证人证词的**一致**精确得可疑——措辞相同、顺序相同、停顿也相同。§con-（一起）+ cord（心，同 cordial 诚恳的）→ 心思对得上
concordant§The instruments gave concordant readings for six hours and then diverged so sharply that the crew assumed one had failed.§仪器在六小时内给出**一致的**读数，随后差异大到船员以为其中一台坏了。§
concur§Three of the five judges concurred in the result while disagreeing entirely about the reasoning behind it.§五位法官中有三位在结论上**意见一致**，而对背后的推理则完全相左。§con-（一起）+ cur（跑，同 current 水流）→ 跑到一处
condemnation§The condemnation was unanimous and the funding was renewed the same week, which told everyone how much the words weighed.§**谴责**是全票通过的，而拨款同一周照常续上，这让所有人明白那些话有多重。§con-（加强）+ damn（判罪）
condemnatory§The condemnatory paragraph was cut before publication, and the version readers saw praises the very practice it once attacked.§那段**谴责性的**文字在出版前被删，读者看到的版本反倒赞美了它原本抨击的做法。§
condense§He condensed a nine-hour deposition into two pages, and the lawyers agreed that nothing important had been lost.§他把九小时的证词**浓缩**成两页，律师们一致认为重要内容一点没丢。§con-（一起）+ dens（稠密，同 dense 密集的）
condescend§She never condescends to the students, which is why they ask her the questions they are too embarrassed to ask anyone else.§她从不对学生**居高临下**，所以他们会向她提那些羞于问别人的问题。§con-（一起）+ descend（下降）→ 屈尊下来
conditional§The offer is conditional on three approvals, and the last of them has historically taken between six and thirty months.§这份录用是**有条件的**，取决于三项批准，而其中最后一项历来要六到三十个月。§
condone§The board condoned the practice for a decade by never asking about it, which its lawyers now describe as oversight.§董事会靠十年绝口不问**默许**了这种做法，其律师如今称之为监督疏漏。§con-（完全）+ don（给，同 donate 捐赠）→ 白送一个赦免
confer§The degree confers no particular privilege, but it is the only credential the licensing board will look at.§这个学位**授予**的特权并不特别，却是执照委员会唯一会看的资历。§con-（一起）+ fer（带来，同 transfer 转移）
confession§The confession was retracted within a day, and the recording shows the interview had run for nineteen hours.§这份**供认**一天内就被翻供，录像显示讯问已进行了十九小时。§con-（完全）+ fess（说，同 profess 声称）
confident§She was confident about the number and wrong about it, and the difference cost the department its entire summer.§她对那个数字**很有把握**，而它是错的，这个差别让部门赔上整个夏天。§con-（完全）+ fid（信任，同 fidelity 忠诚）
configuration§The configuration of the room decides the meeting: a long table produces speeches, and a circle produces argument.§房间的**布局**决定会议的样子——长桌产生演讲，围坐产生争论。§con-（一起）+ figur（形状，同 figure 图形）
confine§The outbreak was confined to two wards, and that containment is the only reason the hospital stayed open.§疫情被**限制**在两个病区，这次封控是医院得以继续开放的唯一原因。§con-（一起）+ fin（边界，同 finish 结束）
conflagration§What began as a kitchen fire became a conflagration that took nine streets and burned for two full days.§一场厨房失火变成了**大火灾**，吞没九条街道，整整烧了两天。§con-（一起）+ flagr（燃烧，同 flagrant 明目张胆的）

conflate§Critics conflate two very different arguments, and the confusion has made the actual disagreement impossible to discuss.§批评者把两种截然不同的论点**混为一谈**，这种混淆让真正的分歧无从讨论。§con-（一起）+ flat（吹，同 inflate 充气）→ 吹到一块儿
conformist§The most conformist student in the seminar wrote the only essay that disagreed with everything the professor had said.§研讨课上最**循规蹈矩**的学生，写出了唯一一篇处处反对教授观点的论文。§
conformity§Conformity here is not enforced but assumed, which makes it far harder to notice and much harder to refuse.§这里的**从众**不是被强制的而是被默认的，因此更难察觉，也更难拒绝。§con-（一起）+ form（形状）→ 变成同一个样子

confound§The results confounded everyone: the control group improved more than the treated group, and nobody could explain why.§结果**让所有人困惑**——对照组比治疗组改善更多，谁也解释不了为什么。§con-（一起）+ found ← fus（倒，同 confuse 混淆）→ 倒到一起搅乱
confusion§The confusion lasted eleven minutes and cost two lives, and the inquiry spent four years explaining those eleven minutes.§这场**混乱**持续十一分钟，代价是两条人命，而调查花了四年解释那十一分钟。§
congenial§She found the department unusually congenial: people read each other's drafts and said what they actually thought.§她觉得这个系**格外投缘**——大家会读彼此的草稿，也会说出真实想法。§con-（一起）+ gen（出生，同 genus 属）→ 天生一路人
conjectural§The dating is entirely conjectural: no inscription survives, and the style could fit any of three centuries.§这个断代完全是**推测性的**——没有铭文留存，风格放进三个世纪里的哪一个都合适。§
conjecture§His conjecture stood unproven for eighty years and then fell to a graduate student with a new computer.§他的**猜想**八十年无人证明，最后被一名带着新计算机的研究生攻破。§con-（一起）+ ject（投掷，同 project 投射）→ 把想法抛出去
conjoin§The two rivers conjoin below the town, and the flood risk everybody worries about lives entirely at that junction.§两条河在镇子下游**汇合**，人人担心的洪水风险全都集中在那个交汇处。§con-（一起）+ join（连接）
connoisseur§A real connoisseur can tell you why the copy fails, and the rest of us can only tell that something is off.§真正的**行家**能告诉你这幅摹本败在哪儿，我们其余人只能感觉到哪里不对。§
conscientious§The most conscientious inspector on the line was moved to another plant three weeks before the recall.§生产线上最**尽责的**检验员，在召回前三周被调去了另一家厂。§con-（加强）+ sci（知道，同 science 科学）→ 心里有数、凭良心
conscript§The government conscripted men up to forty-five that winter, and the village lost every teacher it had.§那年冬天政府**征召**了四十五岁以下的男子，村里失去了所有的教师。§con-（一起）+ script（写，同 script 剧本）→ 把名字写进名册
consecrate§The bishop consecrated the ground in 1782, and the town has argued about who may be buried there ever since.§主教于 1782 年**祝圣**了这片土地，此后镇上一直在争论谁可以葬在那里。§con-（完全）+ sacr（神圣，同 sacred 神圣的）
consecration§The consecration took four hours, and the choir that sang at it had been rehearsing since the previous spring.§这场**祝圣礼**持续四小时，献唱的唱诗班从上一个春天就开始排练。§

consequential§The decision looked small and proved consequential: it set the precedent every later case has been argued against.§这个决定看着小，事实证明**影响重大**——它立下了此后每桩案子据以争辩的先例。§con-（一起）+ sequ（跟随，同 sequence 序列）→ 后果跟着来
conservatism§Institutional conservatism saved the archive twice and nearly destroyed it once, depending entirely on what was being resisted.§机构的**保守**两次救了这座档案馆，也险些毁了它一次，全看抵制的是什么。§

conserve§The trust conserves the wetland by doing almost nothing to it, which took twenty years to persuade anyone was a plan.§这家信托靠几乎什么都不做来**保护**这片湿地，花了二十年才让人相信这也算方案。§con-（完全）+ serv（保持，同 preserve 保存）
considerable§A considerable share of the budget goes to a program the council has never formally evaluated.§预算中**相当可观**的一部分流向了一个议会从未正式评估过的项目。§
consign§The museum consigned four hundred works to storage, and thirty years later nobody could locate eleven of them.§博物馆把四百件作品**交存**入库，三十年后其中十一件谁也找不到了。§con-（一起）+ sign（标记）→ 签好单子交出去
consistency§Consistency matters more than brilliance here: a mediocre routine done daily beats an excellent one done occasionally.§在这里**持之以恒**比才华更重要——平庸的习惯天天做，胜过卓越的做法偶尔为之。§
console§Nothing could console him for the loss of the notebooks, which held thirty years of observations and no copies.§失去那些笔记本让他**无从安慰**，里面是三十年的观测记录，且没有副本。§con-（加强）+ sol（安慰）
consolidate§The firm consolidated eleven regional offices into three, and the savings vanished into the cost of relocating everyone.§公司把十一个地区办事处**合并**为三个，节省下的钱又消失在搬迁所有人的成本里。§con-（一起）+ solid（结实）→ 并成一块
consonance§The finding is in consonance with three earlier studies, which is reassuring and also slightly suspicious.§这一发现与此前三项研究**相合**，令人安心，也稍稍可疑。§con-（一起）+ son（声音，同 sonic 声音的）→ 声音合得上

consort§He consorted with the very lobbyists his committee was investigating, and the photographs ended the inquiry and his career.§他与自己委员会正在调查的说客**来往密切**，那些照片终结了调查，也终结了他的仕途。§con-（一起）+ sort（命运／一伙，同 sort 种类）

conspicuous§Her absence was conspicuous: every other department head sat in the front row, and her chair stayed empty all morning.§她的缺席**十分显眼**——其他部门主管全坐在前排，她的椅子空了一上午。§con-（完全）+ spic（看，同 inspect 检查）→ 一眼就看见
conspirator§The chief conspirator turned witness, and the trial that followed convicted the other eight in under a week.§主要**同谋**转做证人，随后的审判不到一周就判定其余八人有罪。§con-（一起）+ spir（呼吸，同 respire 呼吸）→ 凑在一起密谋

constellation§A constellation is not a group of neighbors: the stars in Orion lie hundreds of light-years apart and only look adjacent.§**星座**并不是一群邻居——猎户座的星彼此相隔数百光年，只是看着挨在一起。§con-（一起）+ stell（星，同 stellar 星的）
consternation§The announcement caused consternation in the department, where four people had been promised the post now given away.§这项宣布在部门里引起**惊愕**——有四个人曾被许诺这个如今给了别人的职位。§con-（加强）+ stern（惊吓）
constitute§Eleven words constitute the entire prohibition, and courts have spent a century deciding what two of them mean.§十一个词**构成**了整条禁令，法院用一个世纪判定其中两个词是什么意思。§con-（一起）+ stitu（建立，同 statue 雕像）

constrain§Budget rules constrain the department far more than the law does, and everyone in it can tell you exactly which rule.§预算规则对这个部门的**约束**远超法律，部门里每个人都能准确说出是哪一条。§con-（一起）+ strain（拉紧，同 strict 严格的）
constructive§The only constructive comment in four pages was a single question about how the data had been collected.§四页里唯一**有建设性的**意见，是一个关于数据如何收集的问题。§
consultation§The consultation lasted six months and changed one word, which the residents' association had asked to change in week one.§这轮**咨询**历时六个月，改了一个词，而居民协会第一周就提出要改它。§

consummate§A consummate committee chair, she could end a two-hour argument with a question that made both sides feel heard.§作为一位**炉火纯青的**委员会主席，她能用一个让双方都觉得被听见的问题终结两小时的争论。§con-（完全）+ summ（顶点，同 summit 峰顶）→ 做到顶
consumption§Household consumption of water fell by a third in one summer, and the utility's revenue fell with it.§一个夏天里家庭用水**消耗**下降了三分之一，供水公司的收入也跟着下降。§con-（完全）+ sum（拿，同 assume 承担）→ 拿光用尽
contagious§His enthusiasm was contagious in a room that had arrived expecting another dull hour of slides.§在一屋子本以为又要看一小时乏味幻灯片的人当中，他的热情**极具感染力**。§con-（一起）+ tag（接触，同 contact 接触）

contemplative§The book is contemplative rather than argumentative: it circles a question for two hundred pages and never settles it.§这本书是**沉思式的**而非论辩式的——它围着一个问题绕了两百页，始终没有定论。§con-（加强）+ templ（观测区，同 temple 神庙）→ 静静观望
contemptible§The excuse was contemptible precisely because it was plausible: he blamed a subordinate who could not answer back.§这个借口**卑劣**恰恰在于它说得通——他把责任推给一个无法辩解的下属。§con-（加强）+ temn（轻视）
